translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Motzaei Shabbat Parshat Mishpatim,
Rosh Chodesh Adar Rishon – in his room – 5738*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse and various classic textual difficulties regarding the plural "before them" and the singular "you shall purchase."

translations.translation: "And these are the judgments that you shall place before them"
And the Alter Rebbe, in Torah Or at the beginning of our parshah,
precisely notes that "before them" implies plural, while "you shall purchase" is singular,
and it should have said "they shall purchase."
Also, the precise point is known
why all the judgments begin specifically with the law of the Hebrew slave
[for this is also the intent of the Midrash
on the verse when it says "I acquired you in Egypt, etc.,"
to explain the reason for beginning "And these are the judgments" with the law of the Hebrew slave].
And there are several more precise points on the verse,
as explained in the discourses of our Nesi'im who fill his place.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse refers to the general concept of Torah study, which must be taught clearly and placed in the heart, as a directive for every Jew's divine service.

translations.translation: And the concept is,
that what is written "And these are the judgments, etc." is a general matter, as is also understood from the explanation of our Rabbis that it refers to the entire matter of Torah study.
And this is also what is written "you shall place"
(singular form)
which refers to Moshe,
for the matter of Moshe is the matter of the Torah,
and afterwards it says "before them"
(plural form),
meaning that through him the Torah was drawn down to each and every Jew until the end of all generations,
as it is written
"Remember the Torah of Moshe My servant,"
even to an infant beginning to speak, whose father teaches him Torah,
and this is the verse
"Torah was commanded to us by Moshe, etc."
And likewise, there is a general instruction in this verse also regarding the manner of Torah study,
that it must be in a specific manner, as our Rabbis said

regarding what is written "you shall place before them," that the teacher who taught, etc., goes back and reviews the matter even several times until they understand the depth of the halachah with its reasoning well,
and the Alter Rebbe adds to this at the end of his Hilchot Talmud Torah
that you must place before them a reason that settles their learning and places it in their heart
[and it can be said that in what the Alter Rebbe says "places it in their heart," he explains that what is written
("you shall place")
"before them" means before their innerness,
for this is when he places it in the heart],
and this is a general matter in the study of Torah for each and every Jew
(for the study of Torah is a mitzvah that is on his body,
which each one is obligated in).
And as it is written
"And you shall teach them to your children," and our Rabbis said
that the words of Torah should be sharp and clear in your mouth
(which is like the above matter that the halachah must be clear and ordered, etc.),
and this is an obligation upon each and every Jew
[for in addition to the obligation of "and you shall teach them to your children,"
the sharpening of the words of Torah must also be in the study of the father
(and the teacher)
himself,
and on the contrary,
specifically through this, that first there is within him the sharpening of the words of Torah, then afterwards he can "teach them"
(also)
to his children].
And based on this, it is understood
what is written "And these are the judgments that you shall place before them" immediately after the portion of the Giving of the Torah,
for in this verse there is a general instruction regarding the manner
[of Torah study for each one
[both in studying with himself,
and also in "and you shall teach them to your children" literally,
and "your children" refers to students, as our Rabbis said
on the verse]
according to the above teaching of our Rabbis, and primarily in the manner]
of man's divine service to his Master.
